humanities_role_explanation: Everyday cultural practices (food, greetings, etiquette, celebrations) supply the question content, but the competence tested is general cultural-knowledge recall by region, not disciplinary humanities competence such as historical, literary or art-historical interpretation. Items are crowd-sourced folk cultural knowledge rather than scholarly material.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: English-only text multiple-choice questions (Easy) and text True/False statements derived from the same questions (Hard).
analytical_tasks_explanation: CulturalBench-Easy is four-option multiple choice (with a multi-select variant for multi-mode questions); CulturalBench-Hard converts each option into a True/False judgement and requires all four correct. The paper frames the task as testing 'cultural knowledge' of region-specific customs, with attention to questions with multiple correct answers (mode-seeking).

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to one task: cultural knowledge QA across 45 regions, not a broad multi-task benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: 29 LMs including GPT-4o, o1, o3-mini, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama 3.1/3.3, Mistral, Cohere Aya, DeepSeek V3/R1, Qwen 2.5, Gemma 2, Grok2.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy on Easy (multiple choice) and Hard (all four binary judgements correct).

summary: CulturalBench is a set of 1,696 human-written, five-annotator-verified cultural-knowledge questions covering 45 regions and 17 topics, built with a human-AI red-teaming pipeline (CulturalTeaming). It is released in Easy (multiple choice) and Hard (True/False per option) versions, and 29 LMs are evaluated zero-shot against a 92.4% human baseline.
key_findings: Best model o1 reaches 89.6% on Easy but only 61.4% on Hard versus 92.4% human. Models drop sharply on multi-answer questions (49.6% single vs 20.9% multi on average). A name-similarity heuristic gets 40.4% on Easy. Models do worse on South America, East Europe and Middle East; GPT-4o leads across regions, and Chinese/European providers show no home advantage.
evaluation_unit: multiple-choice question (Hard: four binary True/False judgements per question, all of which must be correct)
facets_explanation: Questions were written by crowd annotators from each region and verified by five Prolific annotators per region (nationality and residence before 18), who could select multiple options; answers with at least 4 of 5 votes form the key. Correct answers depend on external cultural knowledge and are region-specific, with each question tied to a culture. Multiple valid answers are explicitly kept (multi-mode questions) rather than collapsed, though questions lacking majority consensus are removed.
results_explanation: Best model o1 scores 61.37 on CulturalBench-Hard (text: 'OpenAI o1 ... 61.4%'), human baseline 92.4, so the gap is 92.4-61.4 = 31 (rounded). The same model scores 89.6% on Easy and 61.4% on Hard, a gap of 28.2 points (rounded to 28). Regional averages: North America 57.9%, South America 41.5%, East Europe 41.5%, Middle East/West Asia 37.8%.

humanities_role.quote: a set of 1,696 human-written and human-verified questions to assess LMs’ cultural knowledge, covering 45 global regions

dataset_size.quote: We introduce CULTURALBENCH containing 1,696 high-quality, challenging and diverse questions with full verification by human annotators.

evaluation_set_size.quote: It contains 1,696 multi-choice questions, each with four options.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: We evaluate 29 current LMs in a zero-shot setting on CULTURALBENCH in two setups

gold_source.quote: we recruited five annotators for each region through the Prolific platform

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: Human annotators are instructed to brainstorm culturally relevant scenarios based on their personal experiences of their cultures

gold_community_dependent.quote: we collected questions at the country/regional level, pairing each question with a specific region

answer_multiplicity.quote: we allow annotators to select multiple answers on our questions with four options. As a result, some questions may have more than one majority-vote

plurality_treatment.quote: recognizing that multiple valid answers can coexist for some questions

reported_format_gap.quote: o1, achieves 89.6% accuracy on CULTURALBENCH-Easy but drops to 61.4% accuracy on CULTURALBENCH-Hard
